content: Children's Hospital of New Orleans is a non-profit pediatric hospital located in New Orleans, Louisiana. The hospital provides a comprehensive range of inpatient and outpatient pediatric care services, including a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), and a parenting education center. As of 2002, the hospital has a capacity of 201 beds and employs over 380 pediatricians and pediatric specialists. Annually, it admits more than 7,000 inpatients and handles approximately 170,000 outpatient visits. The hospital serves the entire state of Louisiana as well as the Gulf Coast region. Children's Hospital operates as a non-profit organization and is managed by an independent board of trustees. It was originally established in 1955 as a rehabilitation center for physically handicapped children under the name Crippled Children's Hospital. In 1976, the facility was expanded into a full-service hospital and renamed to its current title. The main hospital is situated in the University District of Uptown New Orleans, at 200 Henry Clay Avenue, New Orleans, Louisiana, 70118. The facility is located along the levee adjacent to the Mississippi River, near Audubon Zoo and Audubon Park. Additionally, there is a satellite clinic in the nearby suburb of Metairie. The hospital is positioned on the city's historic high ground, often referred to as the sliver by the river, which avoided the extensive flooding that affected most of New Orleans during the levee failures following Hurricane Katrina in 2005. The hospital is equipped with its own power generator and remained operational throughout the hurricane. However, it was evacuated on September 1, 2005, when the city lost water pressure. Despite the storm, the hospital sustained no flood damage and only minimal wind damage. It fully reopened on October 10, 2005, just over a month after the hurricane.
